Closes #3479

## What changed

The AI now reads a second fact at a decision's root, `Prices.unknown_root`, beside the Starship one from R3038003. It is set when more than `LEARNED_MAX_UNKNOWN_SHARE` (0.5) of the card copies in the seat's redacted view are ids the network has no row for. When it is set, `finalist_score_with` returns the hand evaluation for every line of that decision, as a Starship root already does.

- **What it counts:** the seat's own hand, both fields and the backrow it can read. It is R3112002's count, `unknown_cards` over `features(&public, seat).sparse`, checked against `known_card_ids()` of the network the search scores with. `plan` passes only `&public` (the redacted view), never `state`.
- **Unknown comes from the network's keys alone.** No set, id prefix or catalog version appears in `learned.rs`, `decide.rs`, `evaluate.rs` or `config.rs`, and a grep of those four files' added lines for `stinky|training|v0.N|prefix` finds nothing. - **The Starship fact stays separate.** The Duos, tutorial and finished-game exclusions are unchanged. A call outside a decision (`Prices::NONE`) carries no fact.
- **Files:** `crates/ai/src/{config,evaluate,learned,decide}.rs`, the new ruling `spec/rulings/R3479000.md` with its paragraph in `spec/pending/3479.md`, a sentence at the end of §9.9's Evaluation bullet, the AI crate's README, and a D9 bullet in `docs/learned-eval.md`.

## The screen

The plan fixed the screen's size and rule before it ran.

- **Control:** built from `3f8896c61d` before any edit. Its `weights.json` names `catalog: v0.3.17`.
- **Arm A** (threshold 0.5): `arena --a self --b bin:/tmp/control-jackioh --set improve-dev`, 400 games over deals `improve-dev:1`–`:200`.
- **Result:** 204–196, no draws, none aborted. Edge +0.020, 95% interval −0.017 to +0.057.
- **Deals:** in 14 deals one side won both games, the switch 9 times and the control 5.
- **Clean games:** no game had `replayOk:false`, a search panic, a fallback or a thrown error.
- **Verdict:** the rule was gain if the interval's low end is above 0, loss if its high end is below 0, even otherwise. This is **even**, so it ships at 0.5 and Arm B (0.75) did not run.
- **What that means:** no gain was measured. The switch ships on R3038003's reasoning: the network's correction of positions it can't read is not evidence. The screen rules out a loss larger than 0.017 edge on the dev set. The ruling and D9 both say this plainly.

## Tests

Four `r3479000_…` tests are at the end of `crates/ai/tests/ai/learned.rs`:
1. **Mostly unknown:** a root whose view is 4 of 5 Training Grounds cards scores every finalist, line and open line by the hand evaluation exactly, while the network does move that board when the fact is off.
2. **Core only:** a Core-only root gets no fact, and the finalist score is still `hand + LEARNED_CORRECTION_SHARE·(points − hand)`.
3. **Hidden cards:** two states that differ only in the enemy hand, a face-down Trap of the same cost and both libraries give the same features, the same count and the same fact. This holds under the test network and the shipped one.
4. **Future card:** `zz-future-001`, an id no set holds, counts as unknown, and as known once a network has a row for it. The threshold behaves as a share at 1, 4, 10 and 1000 named cards.

The tests ask a fixture network (`learned-tiny.json`, fitted on v0.3.1) which ids it lacks instead of trusting a set name. Retraining `weights.json` therefore cannot break them or make them pass for the wrong reason, which is what the maintainer asked for.

- **Shipping on "even".** The plan read "If the network still helps at every share, ship no switch" as: ship unless the screen shows a loss. I rejected the stricter "keep only if `edgeLow > 0`" from `improve.md`; under it nothing would ship.

# #3479: Patch: the practice AI scores a decision by its hand evaluation alone when most of the cards in view are ones its learned network never saw
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI and the ladder bots judge positions partly with a small trained network. It was trained before the Stinkyscape and Training Grounds sets reached AI decks, so it has never seen any of their cards, yet it still gets half the say in every decision. About four in ten of the cards in today's AI decks are cards it has never seen. Once this is built, a decision on a board made mostly of such cards is scored by the hand-written evaluation alone, as decisions involving a Starship already are, until a person retrains the network.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/learned/weights.json` names `catalog: v0.3.17`. Of its 2,927 keys, none names a Stinkyscape or Training Grounds card. Counted from the file: Core 680, Classic 460, Classic+ 608, Meditative 1,000, Meditative+ 135.
- It applies at `LEARNED_CORRECTION_SHARE = 0.5` (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:707`) in every 1v1 decision. The only exclusions are a finished game, Duos, the tutorial's opponent and a Starship root (`crates/ai/src/learned.rs:312-318`).
- R3038003 found this same network, fitted before a set existed, flipping a removal choice by 27 points, and fixed it for Starship decisions only: 'the exception stays right until it has seen a Starship'.
- Measured in this survey: 494 of 1,200 cards dealt into AI decks (41.2%) are unknown to the network, from 16% to 64% per deck. When it was promoted its whole benefit was small (`config.rs`: +0.010 edge for the full correction and +0.064 at half, over 1,600 paired games), and that was measured before these sets.
- `unknown_cards` and `Learned::known_card_ids` (`learned.rs:96-153`, R3112002) already count this share for `cargo jackioh positions`, but no decision reads it.

## Proposal

- At a decision's root, beside `holds_starship` (R3038003), compute with `unknown_cards` the share of named cards the network has no row for. Count only what the redacted view shows (own hand, both fields, face-up backrow), so two states that differ only in hidden cards get the same answer.
- Above a new `LEARNED_MAX_UNKNOWN_SHARE` in `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, a root fact makes `finalist_score_with` return the hand evaluation for every line of that decision, as the Starship root does.
- Pick the threshold by a screen of hand against learned on today's pool (`cargo jackioh arena`, as `training/improve.md` describes) and record its games, seeds and result in the ruling. If the network still helps at every share, ship no switch and report that.
- Write a new ruling widening R3038003's reach, with its tests in `crates/ai/tests/ai/learned.rs`.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/learned.rs`, the root's prices in `crates/ai/src/decide.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/learned.rs`; SPEC §9.9 (`spec/09-architecture.md`); a new ruling note.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test: a root whose view holds mostly Training Grounds or Stinkyscape cards scores every finalist by the hand evaluation exactly.
- [ ] A test: a Core-only root scores as before (the network's correction at its share).
- [ ] A test: two states that differ only in hidden cards (the enemy hand, both libraries, face-down cards) give the same root fact.
- [ ] The screen's games, seeds and result are in the ruling, and `cargo jackioh gate` passes at smoke size.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, clippy, fmt and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.

## Size and risks

Hard, about 5 files and a ruling. The threshold decides how often the network runs at all, and a screen of a few hundred games takes hours on a 4-core machine. This is a stopgap: retraining the network on today's catalog is a person's call (`training/README.md`), and once that is done this switch rarely fires.
